text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Socialist party outlines economic aspects of electoral platform. Leader Lionel Jospin says would impose new tax on businesses linked to payrolls to finance creation of some 350,000 jobs in the private sector.
-- President Jacques Chirac begins a four-day state visit to China today.
-- Cabinet meeting adopts reforms presented by Finance Minister Jean Arthuis on Wednesday aimed at increasing the state's control of state-owned firms.

-- Former Finance Minister Alain Madelin expresses reservations about planned cuts in labour charges included in the centre-right coalition's electoral platform, calls for some flexibility to be applied to minimum wage.
-- Credit Foncier governor says bank needs eight to 10 billion francs to rebuild shareholder equity.
-- Credit Agricole subsidiary Indosuez Carr Futures buys futures activities of broker Dean Witter.
-- Lagardere managing director Noel Forgeard and Matra Marconi Space chairman Armand Carlier say plan to develop Thomson-CSF if win bid for its privatisation, deny planning any dismantling.
-- Strike by traffic controllers at SNCF railway operator to hit most of rail network today.
-- French car and tire manufacturers report higher first quarter sales as growth from foreign activities offsets sluggish domestic market.
